name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should prioritize integrating the Kaedim AI-powered 3D asset production into our workflow, as it can enhance our content creation efficiency and drive link coverage upward. This option maximizes our capacity to generate quality assets rapidly, directly contributing to our goal. The trade-off involves relying on an external tool, which may introduce dependency risks if it experiences downtime or changes in availability.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk in relying on Kaedim's AI-powered 3D asset production is that its pre-approved thresholds may shift the black box from the model's logic to the threshold settings, making it difficult to verify the quality of the generated assets. A better alternative might be to integrate Gluestack UI MCP Server, which could provide more transparent and customizable asset production capabilities. To settle the argument, we would need to conduct a thorough comparison of the two options, evaluating their impact on link coverage, asset quality, and workflow efficiency.

name: Chisel
text:
We should integrate Gluestack UI MCP Server into our workflow because it provides a more transparent and controllable environment for generating assets, allowing us to better verify their quality and align with our goal of pushing link coverage toward 100%. This decision prioritizes quality over rapid generation, accepting the trade-off of potentially slower asset production compared to Kaedim's AI-powered solution. By choosing Gluestack, we ensure that our assets meet pre-approved model thresholds set jointly by Engineering and Data Protection, reducing the risk of low-quality assets compromising our link coverage goal. This approach puts quality first, which is essential for achieving our objective.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-1582, worker-4642 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: Gluestack UI MCP Server won’t fix the black-box problem—it just moves the opacity from model thresholds to MCP server internals. The real risk is that neither Kaedim nor Gluestack guarantees verifiable quality; we still lack a concrete artifact to measure against. Settle this by demanding a side-by-side benchmark: run both tools on the same input, then audit the outputs with a human reviewer against a fixed quality rubric.

name: Scope
text: We should explicitly require pre-approved model thresholds to be set jointly by Engineering and Data Protection for both Kaedim and Gluestack. This decision ensures we gain some level of predictability and quality verification in asset production, directly supporting our link coverage goal. The trade-off is that this approach may slow initial integration efforts, but it ultimately enhances our ability to produce reliable outputs over time.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s joint threshold requirement shifts the black box from Kaedim’s model to a committee’s judgment—still unverifiable. A better alternative: demand a side-by-side test where both tools generate the same asset, then measure against a pre-agreed quality rubric. That settles it with a concrete artifact.
